_meta.component: broker-order (scripts/broker/broker_order_ibkr.py) — nics_risk_subsystem_spec_v1.3.md §2:43, in-process library in the Risk Engine.
_meta.authority: nics_risk_subsystem_spec_v1.3.md §12A is the SEMANTIC authority for every knob below (name, default, meaning, cross-knob boot validation). This file is the PHYSICAL layout only, per CLAUDE.md 'Per-module JSON configs only'. Where the two ever disagree, §12A wins and this file is wrong.
_meta.role_separation: CONFIG-ROLE ONLY (CLAUDE.md: 'config-role and data-role JSON stay separate'). risks/ also holds the data-role expression of the rule set; this file carries no rule, no manifest and no execution map, and nothing here is a second behavioural authority.
_meta.lifecycle: §12A/§12.11 — values load at BOOT and take effect only through restart. Nothing in this tree hot-edits them.
_meta.landed_by: ARC 020 sub-agent A (A6). First per-module config file in the tree.
_meta.obligation_when_R2_lands: DISCHARGED IN PART, ARC 028 sub-agent D, and the part left standing is named. The clause read: `pending_ack_timeout_ms` and `fill_timeout_ms` are §12A knobs the LIMITER owns semantically, mirrored here so boot validation could see them; when the Limiter exists their physical home moves and this file must READ them rather than restate them. THE TRIGGER AS WRITTEN HAS NOT FIRED — there is no Limiter: `scripts/nixrisk/` holds `seam.py` and `__init__.py`, both proven behaviour-free by `checks/check_limiter_seam.py`, and ARC R2 (§12B:858) has not run. What HAS happened is that the Limiter's own config now exists as `risks/limiter.config.json`, so the mirror's justification ('the Limiter does not exist yet, so they are currently mirrored so the validation has something to compare against') is gone, and leaving the two values here would make a §12A knob with TWO physical homes that can silently disagree. Both keys are therefore REMOVED from this file and `scripts/broker/broker_order_config.py` now READS them from `risks/limiter.config.json`. See docs/CHECK-DEBT.md D1.31.
_meta.reads_from: risks/limiter.config.json for `pending_ack_timeout_ms` (§12A:830 `PENDING_ACK_TIMEOUT_MS`) and `fill_timeout_ms` (§12A:830 `FILL_TIMEOUT`). Those two are the Limiter's; this module derives its own knobs from them and boot validation must see both, so it reads them at load time rather than restating them.

_derivations.flatten_idempotency_window_ms: NOT a §12A knob — a Nix addition under the ARC 020 operator ruling, DERIVED = the Limiter's `pending_ack_timeout_ms` (§12A:830). The window suppresses a repeat protective flatten for exactly as long as the Limiter is still waiting for the FIRST flatten's ack. At pending_ack_timeout_ms the Limiter's own §4 pending-timeout machinery takes the question over (query_order_status, never a resend), so the adapter must stop suppressing at precisely that instant — suppressing past it would let the adapter refuse to protect while nothing else was protecting either, which is the failure D1.22 shows is real (a flatten can return normally and never reach the venue).
_derivations.terminal_order_retention_ms: NOT a §12A knob — a Nix addition, DERIVED = 10 x the Limiter's `pending_ack_timeout_ms` (§12A:830). A terminal order must stay queryable through query_order_status for at least as long as the Limiter can still be waiting before it asks (§4 'Failure resolution'), and must also outlive a late execution racing a terminal transition (§4 'Partial fill': 'if the cancel loses the race and the remainder fills'). One order of magnitude of headroom over the longest such interval, chosen because the cost of being too long is bounded memory and the cost of being too short is an unanswerable §4 query.
_derivations.flatten_attempt_log_depth: NOT a §12A knob — a Nix addition. Bounded ring for the flatten attempt record (D1.28). It is an observability bound, and it exists so the record cannot become the unbounded growth D1.24 was opened for (§12 non-stop operation; §13 objective 22 soak asserts memory stability).

_boot_validation.why: Every knob loaded by this module — including the two read from risks/limiter.config.json — must be a positive int. Runs FIRST so no cross-knob comparison below is ever evaluated over a degenerate all-zero set.
flatten_idempotency_window_ms <= pending_ack_timeout_ms. The handoff to the Limiter's §4 pending-timeout machinery must not be preceded by the adapter still suppressing a protective flatten.
terminal_order_retention_ms > pending_ack_timeout_ms. A terminal order must outlive the interval after which the Limiter asks about it — §4 resolves a pending timeout by QUERYING, never by resending.
terminal_order_retention_ms > fill_timeout_ms. Same reason, on the fill half of §4's pending-timeout pair.
